doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Day gigs: weddings and bar mitzvahs versus word processing
summary: He did weddings and bar mitzvahs rather than office work.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Did you ever have to work day gigs?
Yeah. And I used to have, the day gig for me back in the beginning was playing weddings and bar mitzvahs, which I didn’t mind that much, because I just don’t care.
You said that yesterday that it was better to do that —
Than to do data entry or something.

Yeah, what is that called, when you’re — there was a word for that — word processing, but you were a something, when you were — a word processor, does that make sense? And there’s nothing wrong with that, believe me. It’s like being a secretary for a corporation. But if you’re a musician and you move to New York, you understand, you leave your family and you move to New York to make it — I don’t know what that means — but make a living at playing your instrument or writing or composing or whatever, dancing. Why the hell would you leave that and go be a word processor? It has nothing to do with people who do it or secretaries, that’s great, I mean they can learn the computer more. I wish I knew more about the computer. That’s not what I’m talking about. I’m just talking about why do you spend forty hours a week and make three hundred dollars at that time, not now, and I can make two-hundred fifty dollars in one wedding and still have a horn in my mouth, and try to pick up the bridesmaid. Sorry baby, that was a long time ago, before I met you.
